h1: 12 The Residence Hotel Bangkok — Free Airport Shuttle, Breakfast Included, From ฿900
intro: If you have an early morning low-cost flight out of Don Mueang — or land late and just need a clean, comfortable room — 12 The Residence Hotel & Apartment is the answer most seasoned budget travelers keep coming back to. This 3-star property sits just 4 km from Don Mueang International Airport (DMK), with a free minivan shuttle to the terminal taking roughly 8 minutes. Spacious rooms, a Japanese-American breakfast buffet, a gym, and an on-site café round out the picture. Rates start from around ฿900/night in low season. The hotel holds a 9.1 score from over 4,000 verified reviews on Trip.com — strong and consistent for this price point.

body.html: The headline draw is the free airport shuttle to Don Mueang. The hotel runs a minivan to the pedestrian bridge connecting to the terminal — guests are deposited at a covered walkway, then walk across to the departure hall. The drive takes around 8 minutes. Crucially, the shuttle runs as early as 4:00 AM (confirmed by multiple reviews), making those teeth-grinding 5 AM check-in flights far less stressful. Two important caveats: this is a drop-off service only — the hotel does not run pickups from the airport — and the van holds just 9 passengers per run, departing once every hour. Book your slot with the front desk immediately after check-in.

The rooms themselves punch above their price tag. A Standard King runs 25 sqm, with a proper king bed, air conditioning, flat-screen smart TV, minibar, fridge, and a private en-suite bathroom. Step up to the Deluxe King or Deluxe Twin and you get 30 sqm; the Suite stretches to a generous 60 sqm — excellent for a layover with family. Every room comes with free Wi-Fi that guests consistently describe as fast. A small but appreciated touch: each guest receives a ฿100 voucher to spend at the on-site Japanese restaurant or cafe on arrival.

The breakfast buffet is a genuine selling point. Expect Japanese-style items alongside Western staples — a combination that surprised guests expecting the usual toast-and-eggs spread. The on-site Japanese restaurant and cafe also serve through the day, so you can grab coffee before an early departure. Beyond dining, the hotel has a gym, coin laundry, free parking, and 24-hour front desk staff who receive consistently high marks for friendliness and helpfulness.
"Huge room, immaculate, free shuttle worked perfectly at 4 AM, staff couldn't have been more helpful — easily the best value near Don Mueang Airport."

The honest downsides are worth flagging. Several reviews mention noisy air conditioning units that hum loud enough to disrupt sleep — not uncommon in Thai hotels, but worth noting if you're a light sleeper. Corridor noise (doors closing, early departures) is another theme. A handful of reviews on Booking.com cite hard mattresses and minor maintenance issues like leaky taps. The hotel also requires a 1,000 baht cash deposit at check-in that catches some guests off-guard — bring the cash. And don't expect a soft, luxurious morning meal: Booking.com reviews note cold eggs and watery juice on some days, though the overall breakfast rating remains positive.

Getting back from Don Mueang Airport to the hotel is straightforward even without a hotel pickup. Grab is the easiest option — set the pin for Soi Saranakom 10, typically ฿80–120 for the short ride. Alternatively, the SRT Red Line train serves Don Mueang station (right next to the airport terminal) and you can alight at the nearest stop then take a short Grab to the hotel, or simply walk roughly 1.5 km if you're not carrying heavy bags.

Rates run from around ฿900/night for a Standard King in low season, climbing to roughly ฿1,100–1,500 for Deluxe rooms or peak travel periods such as Thai public holidays and school breaks. The score of 9.1 from over 4,000 reviews on Trip.com, combined with an 8.3 on Booking.com (1,297 reviews) and 9.1 on Agoda, tells a clear story: this is a reliable, well-run transit hotel that delivers on its core promises — proximity to DMK, a free shuttle, and rooms that are clean and spacious for the money.

honestSummary: 12 The Residence Hotel is the go-to transit stay for Don Mueang low-cost flyers — free airport shuttle, buffet breakfast, spacious rooms, and a reliable 9.1 score at a price that's hard to beat. Trade-offs are a noisy AC in some rooms, occasionally firm mattresses, and a shuttle that runs outbound only.
honestChecks: If you need a pickup from the airport — the free shuttle is outbound (hotel to airport) only. For the return, use Grab (฿80–120), a meter taxi from the airport queue, or the SRT Red Line train from Don Mueang station (~1.5 km from the hotel).

If you're a light sleeper — some rooms have loud AC units and corridor noise from early departures is real. Ask for the quietest available room at check-in and consider bringing earplugs, especially for a 4 AM wake-up.
If you plan to use the airport shuttle — seats are limited to 9 per run, and runs are hourly. Book your slot at the front desk as soon as you check in — don't leave it until the morning of departure.

faqTitle: FAQ — 12 The Residence Hotel Bangkok (Don Mueang Airport)

faq.q: How far is 12 The Residence Hotel from Don Mueang Airport?
faq.a: The hotel is approximately 4 km from Don Mueang International Airport (DMK) — about 8 minutes by the hotel's free minivan shuttle. The SRT Red Line's Don Mueang station is also around 1.5 km away for those who prefer the train into the city.

faq.q: Is the airport shuttle free? What time does it run?
faq.a: Yes, the airport shuttle is free for all guests. It runs from early morning — guest reviews confirm service as early as 4:00 AM, making it ideal for dawn departures. The shuttle operates once per hour and carries a maximum of 9 passengers per run. Book your seat with the front desk immediately after check-in. Note: the shuttle is outbound only — it drops you at the airport but does not pick up arriving guests.

faq.q: How do I get from Don Mueang Airport back to the hotel?
faq.a: The hotel shuttle does not run pickups from DMK. Your best options are: Grab (easiest, typically ฿80–120 for the short distance), a meter taxi from the official taxi queue inside the terminal, or the SRT Red Line train from Don Mueang station (adjacent to the terminal) to the nearest station, then a short Grab to the hotel.

Breakfast is included in select room packages — typically those booked as room + breakfast. The buffet features Japanese and American items. If you book a room-only rate, breakfast can be added separately. The hotel also has an on-site Japanese restaurant and cafe for other meals.

faq.q: What is the cash deposit requirement at check-in?
faq.a: The hotel requires a 1,000 baht cash security deposit at check-in, refunded on departure. This catches some guests off-guard — bring the cash so you don't have to find an ATM after landing from a late-night flight.
